answer: Like a ridge that forces every climber through one narrow pass, an agent economy can require each identity to lock a refundable stake before it may trade. A lotus grows only where its roots are anchored, and likewise an agent's reputation must be rooted in that locked bond: misbehavior burns part of the stake, like an ember eating its fuel. One person running a hundred fake agents must fund a hundred stakes and risk losing all of them, so creating Sybils costs real money while honest agents keep their bond intact.
